desc:
Build a string t = a + b where a is a prefix of s (possibly empty), b is a suffix of s (possibly empty), and a and b do not overlap in s, i.e. |a| + |b| ≤ |s|. Among all such t that are palindromes, return the length of the longest one.

For example, "abcdfdcecba" gives 9 (take a = "abcdfdc" and b = "ba", giving the palindrome "abcdfdcba"); "abbaxyzyx" gives 5 (a empty, b = "xyzyx"); "abc" gives 1.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: First deal with the characters that already mirror each other at the two ends of s.
Let k be the largest number such that s[i] == s[n-1-i] for all i < k. If these pairs cover the whole string, the answer is n. Otherwise it is always optimal to take those k letters on both sides.

After that, the palindrome continues in the middle part m = s[k..n-k-1] using either only a prefix of m or only a suffix of m. You need the longest palindromic prefix and the longest palindromic suffix of m, which a prefix function (KMP) on m + '#' + reverse(m) gives in linear time.
editorial: Count the matching outer pairs: k is the length of the longest prefix such that s[:k] is the reverse of s[n-k:], with k limited to n / 2. If the matching covers everything, s is a palindrome and the answer is n. Otherwise, the first and last letters of the middle part m differ. Using fewer than k outer pairs can only lose length (any palindrome using a shorter outer part can be extended to use all k), so the answer has the form 2k plus the best palindrome inside m built from just a prefix of m or just a suffix of m: because the ends of m mismatch, a palindrome a + b cannot use letters from both sides of m.

The longest palindromic prefix of m is found by computing the KMP prefix function of m + '#' + m[::-1]; its last value is the longest prefix of m that equals a suffix of the reversed string, i.e. a palindromic prefix. Doing the same with the reversed string gives the longest palindromic suffix. Answer: 2k + max(prefixPal, suffixPal). Time and space are linear.
